popCulture.title: Bibliotheca
popCulture.creator: Apollodorus
popCulture.description: Apollodorus names the naiad Periboea as consort of Icarius and mother of Penelope — the Spartan spring-nymph behind Odysseus' faithful wife.

popCulture.title: Penelope
popCulture.description: Periboea's daughter by Icarius — the queen of Ithaca whose maternal stem is the Spartan naiad, not the Calydonian or Corinthian Periboeas.

popCulture.title: Icarius (Spartan)
popCulture.description: Periboea's husband — father of Penelope who races the suitors and follows his daughter's bridal car in tears.

popCulture.title: Odyssey
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Homer's Penelope is daughter of Icarius; later genealogists supply Periboea as the naiad mother who completes the Spartan stem.
